articles.title: Who is Kevin Sosa? The 12-year-old Dominican prospect linked to a reported $4 million Tigers deal
articles.standfirst: Detroit reportedly reached a massive pre-agreement with a player who cannot officially sign for another four years
articles.summary: Detroit reportedly reached a massive pre-agreement with a player who cannot officially sign for another four years
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers reportedly have their eyes on one of the most unusual prospects in international baseball: Kevin Sosa , a 12-year-old Dominican infielder who is at the center of a reported $4 million future agreement.

The figure immediately stands out, but so does Sosa's age.

Detroit has not officially signed the youngster to a professional contract, because Major League Baseball 's international rules do not allow a player his age to do so.

Under the current system, an international amateur must turn 16 before signing and must be 17 before Sept. 1 of the following year. Players also have to register with MLB before becoming eligible.

Instead, the reported arrangement is a pre-agreement, an informal commitment between a young player, his representatives and an MLB organization that establishes the expected terms of a future signing.

International baseball reporter Wilber Sanchez reported that the Tigers had reached such an agreement with Sosa for a $4 million signing bonus. Sánchez described the amount as historic for a player of Sosa's age and said the youngster is viewed as an elite talent.

“ Sosa is regarded as an elite talent with the tools and projection that would make him highly coveted by any of MLB’s 30 organizations. He already shows an advanced ability to handle fastballs in the 91-93 mph range,” Sanchez reported.

That evaluation helps explain why Detroit would be willing to make such an extraordinary commitment so far ahead of the player's eligibility. But it is important to separate what is known about Sosa from what remains projection.

There is currently limited publicly available information about his playing career, statistics and physical development.

The reports identify him as a Dominican prospect and describe him as an infielder, while Sanchez's scouting assessment highlights his ability to handle significant velocity despite his age.

The 91-93 mph range is particularly notable for a 12-year-old hitter. Still, there is a considerable distance between showing advanced skills at 12 and becoming a professional baseball player.

Sosa could change dramatically over the next four years. His physical development, position, offensive approach and athletic profile could all evolve before he reaches the point at which he can actually sign.

Why Sosa's reported agreement is causing so much attention

The idea of an MLB organization identifying young talent years before the official signing period is not entirely new in the Dominican Republic.

ESPN reported earlier this year that teams have been making informal commitments to international players at increasingly younger ages, with sources telling the outlet that some pre-agreements have involved players as young as 11.

That makes Sosa's age unusual, but not unprecedented within the broader practice. What separates his reported case is the size of the proposed bonus.

“It’s straight lunacy,” said Junior Noboa , executive director of the Dominican Republic’s baseball commissioner’s office. “I spent almost 30 years signing players. Never did I think you’d start seeing 12-, 13-year-old kids signing.”

The system creates obvious uncertainty. Because a player cannot formally sign at 12, an agreement made years before eligibility does not carry the same certainty as an official MLB contract.

A young prospect can develop differently, another organization can emerge as a better fit, or the rules governing international baseball can change before signing day. That uncertainty is central to Sosa's story.

The Tigers reportedly are not handing a 12-year-old $4 million today. Rather, they are betting that the player they see now will continue developing into the prospect they believe he can become when he reaches the legal signing age. That is an enormous projection for any baseball organization.

The reported $4 million also needs to be viewed against the existing international market. Detroit's 2026 international bonus pool was $7.3571 million, according to MLB, meaning the reported Sosa figure would represent more than half of that year's allocation.

But that comparison should not be interpreted as saying Detroit is taking $4 million out of its 2026 pool for Sosa . He would become eligible years from now, meaning his eventual signing would fall under the rules and bonus structure in effect at that time. And those rules could change significantly.

MLB owners have proposed a major overhaul of amateur acquisition, including an international draft.

One proposal would create a 12-round international draft and raise the minimum age for international players to 18. The broader changes are part of negotiations over baseball's next collective bargaining agreement.

If those changes become reality, Sosa's eventual path to professional baseball could look very different from the one that exists today.

For now, the Tigers appear to be betting on a player who remains years away from officially joining their organization.

Sosa's reported $4 million pre-agreement is therefore less about what Detroit has already acquired and more about what the club believes he could become. The next four years will determine whether that projection holds.

Until then, Kevin Sosa is not officially a Tigers player. He is a 12-year-old prospect with a reported seven-figure future waiting for him, provided both he and the baseball system around him develop as expected.

articles.title: Tears at Comerica: Verlander's final pitch gives way to heartwarming mound moment with daughter
articles.standfirst: After more than 20 years in MLB, it was his daughter’s mound visit that brought the veteran pitcher to tears
articles.summary: After more than 20 years in MLB, it was his daughter’s mound visit that brought the veteran pitcher to tears
articles.body:
Justin Verlander had already heard the ovation, soaked in the atmosphere and delivered one last competitive start for the franchise where his major league career began.

Then his daughter appeared. With one out in the sixth inning of Saturday’s game against the Pittsburgh Pirates , Tigers manager AJ Hinch walked toward the stands and brought seven-year-old Genevieve onto the field.

She ran to the mound to take the ball from her father, turning Verlander ’s final pitching change into the most emotional moment of his farewell. The tears came later when Verlander tried to explain what it meant.

“I gave everything for this,” he said. “I left home when she was in school and I wasn’t there. She means the world to me. My family means the world to me.”

The numbers were still impressive. At 43, and after spending much of the season dealing with hip and hamstring injuries, Verlander returned to throw 5 1/3 innings.

He allowed two runs on five hits, walked one and struck out six. That brought his career strikeout total to 3,560 and left him with a final record of 266-159 across a career that began in 2005.

Yet none of those milestones carried the emotional weight of seeing Genevieve walk toward him. His wife, Kate Upton , said the day brought together the parts of Verlander ’s life that mattered most.

“It was a really emotional day, and the things that mean the most to him were together in one place,” Upton said. “I think that’s what made it so special.”

Comerica Park gave Verlander one last reminder of home

Saturday also gave Verlander a chance to reconnect with the atmosphere that defined so much of his first Tigers stint.

“The vibe in the stadium, from the second I walked out there, was just really incredible,” Verlander said. “It brought back some really fond memories of the days when this ballpark was absolutely raucous every single night.”

He pitched for Detroit from 2005 through 2017 before returning for a brief second stint late in his career. This was his first start at Comerica Park in a Tigers uniform since August 2017.

Detroit made sure ending felt complete

The Tigers trailed 3-1 in the ninth inning, leaving Verlander in line for the loss. Then the game turned. Max Clark singled, Hao-Yu Lee doubled and Kevin McGonigle brought home a run before Eduardo Valencia hit a two-run walk-off homer to give Detroit a 4-3 victory.

It was a fitting finish, but even the comeback could not overshadow the defining image of the day. Verlander ’s career included championships, Cy Young Awards, no-hitters and thousands of strikeouts.

His final exit from a major league mound was handed to him by his daughter. That was the moment that mattered most.

articles.title: Kate Upton's drastic decision following Justin Verlander's retirement from baseball
articles.standfirst: Verlander brought his World Series-winning career to a close on September 26.
articles.summary: Verlander brought his World Series-winning career to a close on September 26.
articles.body:
Kate Upton has made her feelings about Justin Verlander ’s retirement very clear, as the former MLB star’s decision to walk away from baseball has brought an unexpected response. Verlander officially closed the book on his 21-year career with the Detroit Tigers , making his final appearance against the Pittsburgh Pirates on September 26 as the emotional farewell included his daughter.

Genevieve threw out the ceremonial first pitch before watching her father take the mound one final time whilst Upton was there for the occasion alongside their children, but days later she revealed that Verlander ’s retirement has also changed her own relationship with America’s pastime. “I’m so excited. I’m never watching another baseball game again,” Upton joked while sitting next to Verlander on the Today show. “It was tears of joy for me." The studio filled with laughter, but it was a moving night at Comerica Park as the 43-year-old took to the mound for his final start as he pitched over five innings against the Pirates. He delivered a characteristically strong performance allowing two runs on five hits while recording six strikeouts in 91 pitches as Detroit eventually won 4-3 and his final outing provided an emotional conclusion. After being removed in the sixth inning, Verlander embraced Genevieve before giving her the baseball from his final MLB pitch and the veteran then walked off the field to a standing ovation with the 34-year-old Upton , watching from the sidelines.

Why Justin Verlander will be so remembered by baseball fans

Verlander leaves baseball with a resume that places him among the most accomplished pitchers of his generation, winning three Cy Young Awards , two World Series titles and 10 All-Star selections. But his longevity was just as remarkable as his individual success as Verlander reached 3,500 career strikeouts, becoming only the 10th pitcher in MLB history to reach the milestone at the time. He finished his career with 3,560 strikeouts, ranking eighth on the all-time list. The right-hander was also a five-time American League strikeout champion and finished among the league's top 10 in innings pitched nine times. His combination of velocity and durability helped define an era of power pitching as Verlander was particularly known for maintaining his fastball late in games. From 2008 onward, he threw pitches exceeding 100mph in the eighth inning or later 44 times, illustrating the unusual endurance that became a hallmark of his career. His retirement closes one of the longest careers of his generation, while Upton 's decision not to watch another baseball game gives the family a humorous footnote to the end of his playing days.
